title: Workspace retrieval requirement
description: The rephraser's output and the retriever's input: what the workspace must be, what it may cost, and the words that find each part of it. It carries NO SKU, NO PRICE of a product and NO PRODUCT NAME, because deciding what is wanted and how to look for it is a different stage from choosing which product supplies it. Every one of the seven categories is always present; `relevant` says whether the customer asked for it.

workspace_intent.description: What the whole workspace is for. Never a search query: the reviewer holds a composed set against it.

total_budget.description: The monthly ceiling on the whole workspace, or nulls when no budget exists. A total is never derived.

is_explicit.description: True when the customer or the application stated it, false when no budget exists.

categories.description: All seven, always present. A category the customer did not ask for is `relevant: false` with empty words.

intentPhrases.description: At most four phrases. Never a product and never a category's search words.

relevant.description: True when the customer asked for this or strongly implied it. An unasked-for category is refused by the composition, not by the rephraser.

retrieval_query.description: One concise sentence stating what the customer needs this thing to do. The slot's purpose, and never a product.

search_terms.description: The words this component's own request implies, as a catalogue would print them.

synonyms.description: Other words a catalogue might use for the same thing.

semantic_concepts.description: Short phrases about purpose, style or situation - uses rather than things.

budget.description: The monthly ceiling on this component. Derived allocations are the rephraser's division of a total and are not to be confused with what a customer stated.

items.description: One to three words a catalogue title could contain. Never a sentence and never a product name.

searchWords.description: At most eight words across search_terms and synonyms together, because more recall than eight buys nothing and costs the ranking.
